title: Applying Bioinformatics to Prostate Cancer Research: A Scoping Review and Novel Research Framework Aligning Datasets, Research Objectives and Bioinformatic Techniques
content:
Background: Bioinformatics has become an essential hypothesis-generating tool in cancer research, expanding in parallel with the rapid growth of high-throughput genomic and clinical data. Prostate cancer research encompasses a heterogeneous ecosystem of datasets spanning large epidemiological cohorts, controlled clinical and prevention trials, specialized intervention studies, and molecular profiling repositories, each with distinct data characteristics and research objectives. Effective translation of these resources into clinical insights requires principled alignment among dataset characteristics, research objectives, and bioinformatic methodology.  This study defines six core bioinformatic techniques (Over-Representation Analysis (ORA), Gene Set Enrichment Analysis/Functional Class Scoring (GSEA/FCS), Pathway Topology Analysis (PTA), Network Topology Analysis (NTA), Individual-level Multi-Omics Pathway Analysis (IMOPA), and Pathway Activity Inference (PAI)), and through a comprehensive scoping review using PRISMA methodology describes how these techniques have been used in prostate cancer research over the past 15 years,

Results: The PRISMA-compliant scoping review summarizes 61 studies in prostate cancer research with results relating to tumor biology (n=29), biomarker discovery (n=42), and novel therapeutics (n=31) with some studies contributing to more than one category. The emerging pattern suggests a persistent translational gap with much of the published bioinformatics literature generating biological knowledge that does not connect to clinical practice in a meaningful way. We then list 14 key prostate cancer datasets within the categories of epidemiological cohorts, clinical and prevention trials, specialized intervention cohorts and molecular profiling datasets and construct a novel framework aligning specific datasets, research objectives and the appropriate bioinformatic techniques. 

Conclusion: The scoping review identifies an emerging translational gap. The constructed framework provides clinicians and researchers with a principled guide for selecting analytical strategies in prostate cancer bioinformatics research and aims to close the persistent gap between biological discovery and clinical impact. As well as promoting understanding and collaboration at the interface of basic science and clinical practice, the framework supports expedited clinical translation to improve individual and population cancer outcomes.
